transcript.content: Hello. What brings you to the clinic today?

I can’t shake this feeling that everything bad that’s happened is my fault and that I’m being punished for it. It’s just this heavy weight I carry every single day, and I don't know how to make it stop.
Have you ever had periods lasting at least a few days where you felt the exact opposite—unusually energetic, happy, or hyperactive, and needing much less sleep than usual?

Oh, no, I’ve never experienced anything like that at all. I’ve never had times of high energy or running around like that. This heavy exhaustion and sadness I’m carrying now is the complete opposite of what you’re describing.
Have you ever experienced a period of deep sadness and exhaustion like this before in your life, or is this the very first time you've felt this way?

No, I've never felt anything like this before in my life; this is the very first time. I used to be so active, but as the first anniversary of my husband's passing approached, this deep sadness and guilt just completely took over. I've never known this kind of heavy exhaustion.
How long have you been experiencing this heavy sadness and exhaustion continuously? Has it been going on for at least two weeks?

Yes, it has been much longer than two weeks—it's been getting steadily worse over the last couple of months. It is there every single day, and this exhaustion makes just getting out of bed feel like I'm dragging a hundred pounds.
Have you also found yourself losing interest or pleasure in the activities and hobbies that you used to enjoy?

Yes, completely. I used to love singing in the choir, tending to my roses, and tutoring the kids at church, but now I just feel entirely numb when I look at those things. There just doesn't seem to be any point in doing any of it without my husband here.
How has your sleep been during this time? Are you having trouble falling asleep, waking up too early, or perhaps sleeping too much?

I fall asleep exhausted, but then I wake up at three or four in the morning with my heart pounding. I just lie there in the dark replaying all my past mistakes, unable to get back to sleep before the sun comes up.
Have you noticed any changes in your appetite or weight recently, such as eating much less or more than usual?

Yes, my appetite is completely gone, and I have to force myself to eat just a few bites of toast or soup because food turns my stomach. My clothes have even started hanging quite loose on me lately, even though I'm not trying to lose weight.

Sometimes when people carry such a heavy weight of sadness and guilt, they might have thoughts of death or feel like they would be better off not waking up. Have you experienced any thoughts like that?
No, I haven't had thoughts of wanting to end my life or wishing I wouldn't wake up. I feel terribly guilty and like I deserve to suffer for my mistakes, but I haven't thought about hurting myself.
Have you found it harder than usual to concentrate, focus on tasks, or make simple decisions lately?

Yes, my mind feels incredibly foggy, and I can't even follow a simple TV show or balance my checkbook anymore. I often find myself just standing in the kitchen holding a bill or a can of soup, completely unable to decide what to do next. It's so embarrassing, and I usually just stay like that until my daughter snaps me out of it.

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient presents with a first-time, severe depressive episode lasting several months, characterized by depressed mood, anhedonia, profound fatigue, early morning awakening, marked appetite and weight loss, excessive guilt, and severe cognitive/decisional difficulties. There is no history of manic or hypomanic episodes, ruling out bipolar disorder. While the onset is related to the anniversary of her husband's death, the severity and number of symptoms meet the full criteria for a depressive episode (F32) rather than a simple adjustment disorder (F43.2). The absence of prior episodes rules out recurrent depressive disorder (F33).
